title: An Exit Interview Nobody Expected to Be Honest
script: Ibu Nur: [professional] Thank you for staying for this, Teguh. Most people simply vanish on their last day, so I appreciate the candour in advance.
Teguh: [wry] I've got nothing left to protect here, which is, I suppose, the one genuine luxury of leaving.
Ibu Nur: [curious] Then let's use it. What would you say actually drove the decision, beneath whatever reason you've listed on the form?
Teguh: [measured] The form says 'new opportunity,' which is true but incomplete, the way most official reasons for leaving tend to be.
Ibu Nur: [gently] What's the incomplete part?
Teguh: [honest] That I stopped believing my work here was actually seen, as distinct from merely being used, which is a distinction I didn't have language for until fairly recently.
Ibu Nur: [thoughtful] That's a sharper distinction than most people offer in these conversations. Can you say more about where that gap actually showed up?
Teguh: [reflective] Every review praised my output in the abstract, yet somehow never translated into advocacy when promotion cycles actually arrived.
Ibu Nur: [honest] I won't pretend that's an isolated pattern. I've watched it happen to others and said less than I should have, at the time.
Teguh: [surprised] I wasn't expecting that admission, frankly, especially not from someone still employed here.
Ibu Nur: [candid] Exit interviews are the one place honesty costs the company nothing, which is precisely why they're so often wasted on scripted pleasantries instead.

Teguh: [considering] Then I'll say the uncomfortable part plainly: the gap between how this place talks about people and how it actually invests in them is wider than anyone in leadership seems willing to acknowledge.
Ibu Nur: [serious] Noted, and I mean that beyond the formality of noting it. What would have changed your decision, hypothetically, six months ago?
Teguh: [thoughtful] Concrete advocacy, once, at a moment when it actually mattered, rather than warm words arriving only after the decision to leave was already irreversible.
Ibu Nur: [sincere] That's a fair, precise answer, and considerably more useful than anything I usually get in this room.
Teguh: [warmly] I don't say it out of bitterness, for what it's worth. I say it because someone after me deserves the advocacy I didn't receive.

quiz.question: Why does Teguh feel able to be candid in this exit interview?
options: He was promised a bonus for honesty
He has nothing left to protect, which he calls the one genuine luxury of leaving
He was ordered to by HR policy
He wants to get another employee fired
quiz.explanation: Teguh says having nothing left to protect is the one genuine luxury of leaving, enabling his candour.

quiz.question: What incomplete reason does the exit form list, according to Teguh?
options: Personal health reasons
'New opportunity,' true but incomplete
Relocation to another city
Retirement
quiz.explanation: The form lists 'new opportunity' as the reason, which Teguh says is true but incomplete.

quiz.question: What distinction does Teguh say he stopped believing was true about his work?
options: That it was ever completed on time
That his work was actually seen, as distinct from merely being used
That it was valued by clients
That it mattered to the company at all
quiz.explanation: Teguh explains he stopped believing his work was actually seen, as opposed to simply being used.

quiz.question: How does Ibu Nur respond to Teguh's observation about the pattern?
options: She denies it ever happens
She admits she has watched it happen to others and said less than she should have
She defends the company fully
She ends the interview immediately
quiz.explanation: Ibu Nur admits she has witnessed this pattern with others and hasn't spoken up as much as she should have.

quiz.question: What does Teguh say would have changed his decision six months ago?
options: A higher salary offer alone
Concrete advocacy at a moment when it actually mattered, rather than words after the fact
Nothing could have changed it
A public apology from leadership
quiz.explanation: Teguh says concrete advocacy at the right moment, not belated warm words, would have changed his decision.
